approvals_flow: Agent hits a gated tool call -> happy-cli parks it pending (for Claude it is built on the Agent SDK canUseTool callback, which can stay pending indefinitely; for Codex/Gemini it is ACP session/request_permission with the four allow/reject option kinds) [agents: canUseTool semantics; ACP permission model] -> happy-cli encrypts the approval event with device-paired TweetNaCl keys and posts it to happy-server, which stores only ciphertext [prior-art: Happy E2E design] -> server fires a push (Expo push -> APNs/FCM) to the store-distributed Happy app [prior-art: Happy push on permission requests] -> lock-screen notification; user taps, app opens the approvals inbox, fetches and decrypts authoritative pending state (never trusts the push payload) -> user taps Approve / Deny or types a steering reply -> encrypted response returns to happy-cli -> the SDK/ACP callback resolves -> agent resumes. The laptop terminal reflects the same resolution via Happy two-way sync and one-keypress device handoff [prior-art: Happy handoff]. iOS backgrounding is safe: no socket needs to survive, because the pending approval lives on the laptop until answered and the app re-syncs on open [phone: iOS suspends sockets; agents: pending canUseTool]. Fallback lane requiring zero of our infra: `/remote-control` mirrors the session to the Claude mobile app with "Push when actions required" approvals [prior-art: Remote Control].

build_phases.scope: brew install tmux (not currently installed) [terminals: local check]; Tailscale on laptop + iPhone (free Personal plan), disable laptop node key expiry day one, VPN On Demand with *.ts.net trigger [transport]; pmset -c sleep 0 + caffeinate LaunchAgent; enable Tailscale SSH; run `claude remote-control` inside a tmux session (process must stay alive) [prior-art: RC limits]; install Claude mobile app; install Blink Shell, connect mosh/ssh over the tailnet, `tmux attach`.
build_phases.deliverable: Same day: approve/deny/steer Claude Code sessions from the phone with push (Claude app), Dispatch for remote Claude kickoff, and full input/output control of any tmux terminal from the phone via Blink. Laptop reachable 24/7. Zero custom code.

build_phases.phase: Phase 2 — Happy hub on hosted relay (~2 days)
build_phases.scope: Install happy-cli; run `happy daemon start` under a launchd LaunchAgent (state in ~/.happy/daemon.state.json); QR-pair the store-distributed Happy app; use Happy's hosted relay (E2E, ciphertext-only server); explicitly never use `happy connect` API-key storage (the #680 hole) — subscription OAuth stays local; wire up Codex and Gemini (--experimental-acp) as Happy agents; shift habit to launching agents via happy or from the phone.
build_phases.deliverable: One phone app showing all AI-agent sessions: approvals inbox with push, steering messages, live streaming output, remote spawn in any project directory, device handoff. Phase 1 Remote Control demoted to fallback.

build_phases.phase: Phase 3 — Terminals with touch UX + VS Code (~1.5 days)
build_phases.scope: Install VibeTunnel (menu-bar + native iOS app), reachable strictly over Tailscale; set VS Code default terminal profile to `tmux new -A -s vscode-N`; set tmux history-limit and a window-size policy in .tmux.conf before creating sessions; enable `code tunnel` as a LaunchAgent escape hatch.
build_phases.deliverable: Touch-friendly view + control of every tmux terminal including VS Code integrated ones (new terminals get persistence for free); full IDE available from the phone browser via vscode.dev when genuinely needed.

build_phases.scope: Run happy-server (standalone Docker image, no external Postgres/Redis/S3) on the laptop via OrbStack/Docker, bound to localhost, published with `tailscale serve` under the ts.net Let's Encrypt cert (auto-renewed); point happy-cli (HAPPY_SERVER_URL) and the app's custom-server setting at it; verify push delivery from the self-hosted server on-device before cutting over; keep hosted-relay config as fallback.
build_phases.deliverable: Identical UX with no third party in the agent data path: all sync device-to-device over WireGuard, zero public endpoints. If self-hosted push fails verification, stay on the hosted relay knowingly (still E2E).

build_phases.phase: Phase 5 (optional, only if two-app UX grates) — Single-app terminals via Happy fork (~6-8 days)
build_phases.scope: Fork Happy (MIT): add a terminal session type — happy-cli side speaks tmux control mode (`tmux -C attach`, %output streaming, send-keys input, capture-pane -p -e -S - replay, pause-mode flow control) over the existing E2E channel; Expo side renders it in an xterm.js WebView per the @fressh pattern (write coalescing, Ctrl/Esc/arrow key row). First re-verify that Happy still lacks this (absence was UNVERIFIED).
build_phases.deliverable: One app is the single remote for agents AND terminals; VibeTunnel/Blink retired to fallbacks. Deferred by default — this is the only real custom code in the design.

laptop_side: All reused components, glued by dotfiles and launchd plists (the only "code" until optional Phase 5): (1) tmux via Homebrew — the single terminal substrate; .tmux.conf sets history-limit before any session exists and a window-size policy; VS Code's default terminal profile becomes `tmux new -A -s vscode-N` [terminals: tmux is the capture layer; history-limit applies only to new windows]. (2) happy-cli daemon (Node, `happy daemon start`, auto-started by a launchd LaunchAgent as the logged-in user; state in ~/.happy/daemon.state.json) — spawns and manages Claude Code (default), Codex, and any ACP-compatible agent, owns approvals/streaming/remote-spawn [prior-art: happy-cli daemon facts]. (3) happy-server, Phase 4 only: the standalone Docker image (no external Postgres/Redis/S3) on OrbStack/Docker Desktop, bound to localhost and published via `tailscale serve` [prior-art: Happy self-host]. (4) VibeTunnel menu-bar app for touch-friendly terminal access, tailnet-only [prior-art: VibeTunnel]. (5) tailscaled + `tailscale serve` (auto-renewing ts.net LE cert) [transport: cert renewal]. (6) claude CLI on subscription OAuth, with `claude remote-control` inside tmux as the fallback lane; DISABLE_TELEMETRY/DO_NOT_TRACK/custom base URL must stay unset or it silently dies [prior-art: RC limits]. (7) Power config: pmset -c sleep 0 (+ caffeinate LaunchAgent) — hard prerequisite, nothing works if the laptop sleeps [transport pitfall]. (8) Optional `code tunnel` LaunchAgent. Node v26 already present; tmux is not — brew install is step one [terminals: local check].
name: Happy-on-Tailnet
not_built: Custom phone app, APNs pipeline, Apple Developer account, TestFlight re-upload churn — Happy, VibeTunnel, Claude, Blink are store-distributed apps whose maintainers carry the $99/yr + push-entitlement burden [phone: paid account mandatory; prior-art pitfall: home-grown app pays it for one user]
Relay server and E2E encryption — happy-server + TweetNaCl device-key pairing reused as-is [prior-art: Happy E2E]
Laptop daemon, Claude Agent SDK integration, ACP client, approvals state machine, session-spawn API — all happy-cli [prior-art: 90% of brief]

VS Code companion extension — research shows extension-side mirroring is best-effort-only anyway (read() attach-at-start, no raw-stream API, webview isolation); tmux default profile + `code tunnel` replace it [vscode facts]

Terminal transport and renderer — no ttyd/GoTTY/tty-share/upterm deployment, no @xterm/headless service, no WebSocket protocol; tmux + VibeTunnel/Blink+mosh cover it [terminals: skip ttyd/GoTTY as components]
Any TUI scraping of agent screens to detect prompts — structured channels only (SDK/ACP via Happy); Omnara's deprecation is the standing warning [prior-art: Omnara]
Public endpoints, Cloudflare Tunnel/Access, bespoke auth/token system — tailnet + Happy QR pairing + Tailscale SSH identity instead [transport: Cloudflare reads plaintext]
Push notification service — Expo->APNs/FCM via Happy's published app; no ntfy piggyback (documented iOS flakiness) [phone: ntfy issues]
Retro-capture of non-tmux PTYs (impossible on macOS; reptyr is Linux-only) — the UI just shows those terminals as not capturable [terminals: fact 6]
Multi-user support, sharing, or any relay hardening beyond single-owner use — out of scope for a personal tool
notifications: Entirely reused: Happy's store-distributed app means APNs/FCM certificates and the $99/yr Apple Developer account are the Happy maintainers' problem — the single biggest cost the glue stance deletes, since a home-grown standalone iOS app cannot have push without the paid program [phone: free accounts have no push entitlement, 7-day builds]. Happy pushes on permission requests and task completion [prior-art: Happy features]; the Claude app pushes for /remote-control sessions ("Push when Claude decides" / "Push when actions required") [prior-art: RC]. Pushes are treated as signals only — the app fetches decrypted authoritative state over its channel, so nothing sensitive rides Expo/APNs in a form third parties can read (Happy payloads are within its E2E design; Expo itself offers no payload E2E) [phone: Expo push transparency]. Two verifications scheduled early on real devices: approval actions from killed state (Android action buttons historically no-op'd) [phone: expo issue history], and push delivery when the server is self-hosted in Phase 4 (assumed from the self-hosting reviewer's report, UNVERIFIED). Escalation if an approval sits unanswered is Happy's behavior to inherit, not ours to build; the guaranteed fallback is always tap-notification -> inbox.
phone_side: iPhone (primary): Happy app from the App Store — Expo/React Native; sessions list, approvals inbox with push, chat-style steering, live streaming, git diff views, remote spawn, device handoff; custom server URL switched to the self-hosted ts.net endpoint in Phase 4 [prior-art: Happy app + self-host reviewer used same apps]. VibeTunnel native iOS app for terminal sessions over Tailscale [prior-art: VibeTunnel remote via Tailscale]. Blink Shell (native mosh) + Tailscale SSH as the raw-terminal fallback that works when everything else is broken [prior-art: Blink/mosh/tmux classic stack]. Claude mobile app for the /remote-control fallback lane and Dispatch kickoff [prior-art: RC facts]. Tailscale iOS app with VPN On Demand *.ts.net hostname trigger (interface rule "Do Nothing") so the tunnel self-raises when any app resolves the ts.net name — no manual VPN toggling, and battery stays fine because the laptop is never an exit node [transport: iOS on-demand + battery facts]. Android parity: Happy ships Android; Termius (mosh via compat library) replaces Blink; Tailscale Android — store installs sidestep the 2026 sideloading verification changes entirely [phone: Android verification timeline]. No custom app is built; if Phase 5 ever happens it is a fork of Happy's existing Expo app, not a greenfield client.
remote_start: From the Happy app: pick a project directory and agent, and the happy-cli daemon spawns the session with no terminal open on the laptop (`happy daemon start/stop/status`, auto-start, state in ~/.happy/daemon.state.json) [prior-art: happy-cli daemon]. Claude sessions spawned this way land in the shared ~/.claude/projects store, so back at the laptop they resume in the CLI with `claude --resume <id>` — with the known constraints: resume is keyed to the encoded cwd, and laptop CLI and daemon must not drive the same session ID concurrently (treat attach as exclusive; concurrency is UNVERIFIED) [agents: session store + resume pitfalls]. Secondary zero-infra path: Claude Dispatch from the Claude mobile app (message a task, Desktop spawns it) [prior-art: Dispatch]. New plain terminal remotely: create a session from VibeTunnel's UI or Blink ssh then `tmux new -A -s name -c ~/project`. Remote spawn is by nature remote code execution on the laptop; the gate is layered reused auth — WireGuard device identity (tailnet) + Happy's QR pairing with device-held keys — and no generic exec endpoint exists beyond what these audited-in-public tools already ship [transport recommendation: typed operations, no public ports].
risks: Happy hosted relay reliability: the public endpoint (api.cluster-fluster.com) has documented timeout episodes — until Phase 4 self-host, a relay outage removes remote agent control (Remote Control and Blink lanes still work) [prior-art: self-hoster's report]

Happy security posture: Discussion #680 showed 'E2E' marketing while `happy connect` API keys were server-decryptable via HANDY_MASTER_SECRET; we avoid that exact hole (no API keys stored, subscription OAuth stays local) but the codebase is not independently audited — self-hosting on the tailnet in Phase 4 is the real containment [transport: Happy #680]

Three load-bearing UNVERIFIED items: (a) Happy lacking plain-terminal sessions (absence unverified — re-check before funding Phase 5), (b) push delivery from a self-hosted happy-server through the store apps (verify before cutover), (c) concurrent CLI + daemon resume of one Claude session (assume single-writer) [prior-art/agents]

Upstream churn: Happy wraps the Claude Code/Codex processes, the exact treadmill that killed Omnara's OSS wrapper — we inherit breakage windows after agent CLI releases and depend on Happy's fix latency instead of owning the maintenance [prior-art: Omnara deprecation]

The 'single remote' brief is met with two apps (Happy for agents, VibeTunnel for terminals); if that UX does not hold up, Phase 5's fork is the exit — and maintaining a fork of a fast-moving Expo monorepo is a real ongoing cost, the one place glue-first can turn into build-anyway

/remote-control fallback is fragile: claude.ai OAuth only, silently disabled by DISABLE_TELEMETRY/DO_NOT_TRACK/custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, directory-bound per server, and transcripts sit on Anthropic servers un-E2E'd [prior-art: RC limits]

The laptop is a single point of failure with no out-of-band recovery: sleep misconfig, power cut, or ISP outage kills everything; pmset + disabled key expiry mitigate the self-inflicted cases only (no remote power control is built)

tmux-only capture is honest but partial: terminals opened outside tmux, or before the VS Code profile change, are permanently invisible (macOS PTY limitation) — the session list must say 'not capturable' rather than pretend [terminals: reptyr not macOS]

Phone tmux attach registers a client size (window-size=latest default) and can shrink laptop panes, and Claude Code's ink TUI demonstrably corrupts on resize — keep agent TUIs viewed through Happy, never through a phone-attached tmux client, and set a window-size policy for shared shells [terminals: ink resize bugs]
First request after VPN idle can time out while WireGuard establishes via the On Demand trigger — expect a retry, not instant connect [transport: on-demand pitfall]
surface_capture: (1) Claude Code sessions — primary: launched/owned by the happy-cli daemon, which drives Claude with structured approvals, streaming, and push; because Claude sessions live in the shared ~/.claude/projects JSONL store, phone-started sessions remain resumable on the laptop with `claude --resume <id>` and vice versa [agents: shared session store; prior-art: happy-cli]. A `claude` the user launches by hand: preferred habit is launching via happy; alternatively that one session uses built-in `/remote-control` to the Claude app (works from CLI and the VS Code extension) [prior-art: RC facts]. A bare Claude TUI inside tmux is still screen-mirrorable as a terminal (VibeTunnel/Blink) but gets no structured approvals — we never scrape the ink TUI, per both researchers' warnings [terminals + agents pitfalls]. (2) Other AI agents — Happy natively supports Codex, agy, and any ACP-compatible CLI, so Gemini CLI via `--experimental-acp` rides the same approvals/streaming pipeline (ACP session/request_permission maps to the same inbox) [prior-art: Happy agents; agents: ACP ecosystem]. Non-ACP agents fall back to a plain tmux terminal, mirror-only, labeled as such. (3) Plain terminals — tmux is the sole capture substrate: any same-user process can attach to the default tmux socket regardless of who started tmux [terminals: fact 5]. Phone access: VibeTunnel (native iOS app, touch UI, tailnet-only) or Blink+mosh then `tmux attach`. Terminals not inside tmux are not capturable on macOS at all (no PTY-master API; reptyr is Linux/FreeBSD only) — the UI shows them as existing-but-not-capturable, honestly [terminals: fact 6 + honesty pitfall]. (4) VS Code itself — no companion extension in this stance: integrated terminals become tmux-visible by setting the default terminal profile to `tmux new -A -s vscode-N` (also giving crash persistence) [terminals recommendation]; the Claude extension chat panel is unreachable by design (webview isolation) so `/remote-control` from the extension is the supported hook [vscode: webview isolation; prior-art]; the full IDE from the phone is the documented escape hatch `code tunnel` -> vscode.dev in the phone browser, kept as a break-glass tool, not a daily surface, given its poor touch UX [vscode: tunnels facts].
thesis: Do not write a platform that a maintained MIT project already ships: Happy (22.9k stars, E2E-encrypted, self-hostable, multi-agent, store-distributed iOS/Android apps) already implements roughly 90% of this brief, so the product is Happy composed with tmux as the universal terminal capture layer, Tailscale as the only network, VibeTunnel/Blink for terminals, and Claude's built-in /remote-control as the zero-infra fallback — custom work is confined to configuration, launchd plists, and (only if the two-app UX fails) an additive terminal-session fork of Happy.
transport: Two layers, both reused. Agent channel: Happy's protocol — TweetNaCl E2E encryption with keys generated on-device, QR one-time-challenge pairing, server stores only ciphertext [prior-art: Happy E2E]; Phases 2-3 it runs through Happy's hosted relay (acceptable interim: payloads sealed, and we never invoke `happy connect` API-key storage, the exact #680 hole — the user's subscription OAuth never leaves the laptop), Phase 4 moves happy-server onto the laptop itself. Network layer: Tailscale free Personal plan (1 user, laptop + phone, well inside limits) [transport: pricing]; the self-hosted server binds localhost and is published only via `tailscale serve` under the laptop's MagicDNS name with an auto-renewing ts.net Let's Encrypt cert — avoiding both the 90-day manual `tailscale cert` trap and iOS ATS exceptions for plain http [transport: cert + ATS facts]; laptop node key expiry disabled day one so it does not silently drop offline at day 180 [transport: key expiry]; phone uses VPN On Demand's *.ts.net hostname trigger (interface rule "Do Nothing") so the tunnel raises automatically [transport: iOS on-demand]. Cloudflare Tunnel was rejected because its edge terminates TLS and reads the plaintext command channel, and a service token in the app is a static bearer credential [transport: CF facts]. Result: zero public endpoints, zero 0.0.0.0 binds, WireGuard device-to-device for everything including SSH/mosh/VibeTunnel, with app-level auth (Happy pairing keys, Tailscale SSH identity) stacked on top.
